description: Out of 60 IPOs that listed between 30 and 60 days ago, 25 companies are currently trading above their original IPO price. 34 companies are currently trading b.

faq.a: An Initial Public Offering (IPO) is when a private company first offers its shares to the public to raise money, allowing ordinary investors to buy a part of the company.

faq.q: How do I apply for an IPO?
faq.a: You can apply for an IPO through your bank's ASBA (Application Supported by Blocked Amount) facility or through your stockbroker's platform, typically using your UPI ID for payment.

faq.q: What is the difference between Mainboard and SME IPOs?
faq.a: Mainboard IPOs are for larger, more established companies that list on the main exchanges (NSE or BSE), while SME (Small and Medium Enterprise) IPOs are for smaller companies that list on dedicated SME platforms of these exchanges, with different rules and regulations.
The "issue price" is the fixed price per share at which a company offers its shares to investors during its IPO.
